title: Title formats per surface (issue, milestone, PR)
description: Formal shape of titles.yaml — one entry per title surface (per-issue-type issue titles, milestone titles, PR titles). Each entry carries a regex `pattern` consumers compile, a prose `description`, examples, and per-rule validations tagged with severities. Issue and milestone titles are read for board browsing; PR titles follow Conventional Commits for `git log` parsing. Read through scripts/_lib/title_rules.py by create-issue, edit-issue, validate-issue, validate-pr and create-milestone. Companion per COR-018.

formats.description: Title-format entries. Keys are surface ids (e.g., `issue-epic`, `milestone`, `pr`); values match $defs.entry.

surface_kind.description: Which surface this title shape applies to. Determines which validations the skill runs (issue → board-browsing checks; pr → Conventional Commits checks).

applies_to_issue_type.description: When `surface_kind: issue`, the issue type whose title this entry governs. Omitted for `milestone` and `pr` surfaces (which apply to a single global surface).

pattern.description: Regex (PCRE-compatible) the title must match. `null` for free-form surfaces (e.g., milestone). A named group `text` marks the part the wording checks read (the title after its prefix, the PR summary). Consumers compile against the language they run in; if the regex must differ across languages, encode the divergence here explicitly.

description.description: One-paragraph prose describing the format — what the parts mean, what readers should expect.

examples_good.description: Titles that match the pattern. Illustrative.

examples_bad.description: Titles that should be rejected and why. Helps consumers verify their regex catches the listed cases.

check.description: The check that enforces the rule. `pattern`: the title matches the entry's `pattern`. `forbid` / `require`: the title's text contains no / a match for `regex`. `min-length` / `max-length`: the text is at least / at most `length` characters. `kind-prefix` (issue titles) and `type-alignment` (PR titles) need the issue's or the closing issues' kind and are run by validate-issue and the PR validator. The text is the pattern's named group `text` when it has one, else the whole title. A rule no check enforces cannot be declared.

name.description: The finding label a violation is reported under (e.g. `title.scope-prefix`).

regex.description: For `forbid` / `require`: the regex searched for in the title's text.

length.description: For `min-length` / `max-length`: the bound on the text's length, in characters.

validations.description: Per-rule validations run against a title on this surface. Each rule is prose paired with the check that enforces it, the finding label, and a severity token; severity dispatch happens via the validation-severity schema. Wording checks (`forbid`, `require`, `min-length`, `max-length`) apply at the declared severity where a title is written; at a lifecycle transition a blocking one reports as a warning.
